purpose: Compares image-only, text-only, and joint (image+text concatenated) classifier heads on the identical train/test split, to verify the joint model is actually doing multimodal fusion rather than being dominated by one modality.
note: An earlier version of the 'misleading' label leaked through a fixed filler breed name ("Persian"/"Labrador Retriever" hardcoded for the wrong species), which let text-only hit 100% recall on that class via keyword matching. Fixed by sampling the filler breed from the full wrong-species breed pool; results below are post-fix.
findings: misleading (image-text mismatch): joint model (0.792 recall) clearly beats both single-modality ablations (image-only 0.292, text-only 0.625). This is the expected result -- detecting a mismatch is inherently relational and needs both modalities present at once. Neither modality alone can 'know' what the other one claims.

policy_violation (banned claim language): this is the one place the joint model does NOT beat the single-modality baseline -- text-only hits 1.000 recall, joint is 0.917. Concatenating image features that carry no information about claim language adds parameters without adding signal for this class, and appears to cost a small amount of recall at the margin. This is reported as-is rather than smoothed over: for a production system, a rule/text-only path for claim-language violations would likely outperform the joint model on this specific category.

low_quality (half image-degraded, half text-degraded): joint model hits 1.000 recall by combining both signals -- neither single modality gets above 0.583 because each one is blind to exactly the degradation type it can't see (image-only misses the text-garbled half, text-only misses the image-blurred half).

image-only accuracy (0.365) is barely above random-guess baseline (0.25) except on low_quality, confirming the image alone carries very little signal for approved/policy_violation/misleading -- those three classes use undegraded, randomly-sampled photos, so there's genuinely nothing in the image alone to distinguish them by construction.

statistical_caveats.note: Test set is 96 examples, 24 per class -- individual per-class recall numbers carry wide 95% Wilson confidence intervals (see model/results/confidence_intervals.json) and should be read as directional, not precise to the decimal point.
statistical_caveats.overall_ranking_is_robust: The three modalities' overall-accuracy 95% CIs do not overlap (image [0.275, 0.464], text [0.589, 0.771], joint [0.819, 0.942]), so the headline ranking joint > text > image is statistically solid despite the small test set.
statistical_caveats.one_number_not_distinguishable_from_chan: image-only recall on misleading is 0.292 with 95% CI [0.149, 0.492] -- this interval contains the random-guess baseline of 0.25, so at n=24 this specific point estimate cannot be statistically distinguished from chance, even though the near-floor performance is exactly what the relational-signal hypothesis predicts.
